Bare-Bones Changelog Podcast

The shortest path from a clone to your first episode, from your own changelog.

Short answer: almost. Clone it, give it an RSS feed, and pick voices is the right shape. Today two more steps are required before it sounds like your show: your segment list and your show's name and outro. You don't need to spend money on test episodes to choose segments. A free dry run shows you a year of your changelog first.

First episode, on your laptop

About an hour, about 20 cents.

  1. Clone and install. Python 3.9 or newer, ffmpeg, and two packages. 
    git clone https://github.com/samgutentag-deepgram/deepgram-changelog-podcast
cd deepgram-changelog-podcast
brew install ffmpeg
pip install anthropic pillow
  2. Add two keys to a .env file (copy .env.sample): DEEPGRAM_API_KEY for the voices and the readback check, and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for the writer.
  3. Point it at your feed. Add CHANGELOG_FEED_URL=https://your-site/changelog.rss to .env. RSS or Atom both work. Each item needs its full post, not a teaser.
  4. Read your changelog for free. This step makes no API calls. 
    set -a; . ./.env; set +a
python3 scripts/backfill_plan.py
open research/backfill-review.html
    You get every week with entries and every entry title. Check that the weeks look right and the entries have real text. Ignore the segment columns: they are keyword guesses tuned for Deepgram. The writer does the real sorting.
  5. Pick your segments. Scan those titles and choose three to six buckets your readers care about. (Or paste the "Plan Your Show With Claude" prompt from the README into Claude Code, and it proposes names, segments, and a cast from your own feed.) Keep "Breaking changes and action required", "Launches", and "Quick hits", which fit any product. Replace "Voice Agent", "Speech-to-Text", "Text-to-Speech", and "Developer experience" with your own. Edit SEGMENTS and SPOKEN_SEGMENT in scripts/write_episode.py, then the same names in RUNNING_ORDER in scripts/make_art.py and SEGMENTS in scripts/build_catalog.py.
  6. Pick voices. In docs/cast.json, set the anchor and, if you want a desk, one Flux TTS voice per segment. Any segment you leave out goes to the anchor, so one voice is a valid cast.
  7. Rename it and rewrite the outro. The name is in TITLE in scripts/build_feed.py, SITE_TITLE in scripts/serve.py, and the SYSTEM prompt in scripts/write_episode.py. The outro (OUTRO_COST, OUTRO_PROMO, OUTRO_HELP) currently plugs Deepgram credits and Deepgram support. For a private first listen you can skip this step, but do it before anyone else hears the show.
  8. Make one episode and listen. Pick a recent Tuesday. The episode covers the Sunday to Saturday before it. 
    python3 scripts/produce.py 2026-09-22
python3 scripts/serve.py    # then open localhost:8010
    Read episodes/<date>/readback.json for any spots the check flagged, and listen there.

Make it a show (optional)

  1. Teach it your hard words. Put product names in docs/key-terms.json and run python3 scripts/term_test.py --voice <voice> once per voice.
  2. Host it. Set SITE_URL, rename app in fly.toml, set the keys with fly secrets set, then python3 scripts/stage_site.py and fly deploy.
  3. Turn on Tuesdays. The crontab runs the weekly job at 5am Pacific. Change CRON_TZ if you want a different morning. Add the two Pushover keys from .env.sample if you want an alert after every run.

Bonus: an llms.txt

If your changelog also publishes an llms.txt index, you can set CHANGELOG_INDEX_URL instead of the feed. The writer then reads each entry as it was written, with no HTML conversion. It adds no entries, so compare the two first: run step 4 once with each and check the entry counts. Deepgram's per-day pages drop the second entry on a two-entry day, which is why this show reads the feed.

The Deepgram Changelog · docs/bare-bones.html · the full list of what to change is in the README under "Fork It For Your Own Changelog".
